findings.issue: Inside the totalAssets loop (inlined in 20 functions) 104 calls show their selector as mem[_N len 4] although the line before stores it at mem[mem[64]] right after '_N = mem[64]', 38 'max uint128 exceeded' reverts stay raw memory (the message is printed as a hex word two lines above), and the library calls lose function and arguments; setCap, where the same code runs at constant offsets, prints market(), position(), borrowRateView() and revert with 'max uint128 exceeded'.
findings.rule: After '_v = mem[64]' with no store to mem[64] in between, mem[64] and _v are the same value: rewrite mem[mem[64] + k] to mem[_v + k] and '_v - mem[64]' to 0; then the selector word, the Error(string) buffer and the argument buffer are read back like constant-offset buffers.
findings.verified: reading only (setCap 2020-2153 vs deposit 8563-8772: same source, decoded only at constant offsets)

findings.issue: The second array argument is printed as its head offset (32 * len + 128) with its length and data appended inside the first Array(...), and the returned value reads as mem[_14], the word where the text stored the selector, because the return data is copied to mem[mem[64]] and mem[64] is not folded to _14 although it was assigned that value before the loop.
findings.rule: Decode an ABI argument list head by head: each head word that is an offset o names a tail at base + o, printed as its own Array(len, data). Fold mem[64] to its last stored value when no store to slot 64 can intervene (loop bodies here write only 32 * idx + 160 + c and slots 0/32).

findings.source: AccessControlUpgradeable._checkRole: revert AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(account, role) for onlyRole(MANAGER/CURATOR/ALLOCATOR)
findings.issue: The custom error's selector and address argument are merged into one word plus a 4-byte tail, so the revert reads as three odd values; for the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE check the same error prints as 'revert with 0xe2517d3f, caller, 0'.
findings.rule: Revert and call data that start with a 4-byte selector are re-split after byte 4: 'sel << 224 | x >> 32, Bytes(4, uint32(x))' is 'sel, x' whenever x < 2^160 (generally: Bytes(a, x >> 8b), Bytes(b, x mod 2^8b) is Bytes(a + b, x)).

notes: via-IR build, 84 decompiled functions for 81 ABI entries (+ fallback). All reviewed; the inlined totalAssets/expectedSupplyAssets/wTaylorCompounded block (~350 lines, repeated in 20 functions) was reviewed once and then by structure. No semantic error found. Loops: the 7 loops of MoolahVault.sol are all whiles: setSupplyQueue:247, updateWithdrawQueue:264 and :275, reallocate:303, totalAssets:470 (inlined 20 times), _maxDeposit:517 (maxDeposit, maxMint), _supplyMoolah:668 (deposit, mint). The 5 loops of MoolahVaultLib (reallocate:40, supplyMoolah:103, withdrawMoolah:138, simulateWithdrawMoolah:172, maxDeposit:205) are in a linked public library reached by DELEGATECALL to 0x1160663e...809890, so they are not in this bytecode and are not counted. Implicit loops: storage-to-memory copies (getWhiteList, getRoleMembers, supplyQueue/withdrawQueue writes, string writes) are copy lines; 12 ABI-encoding loops over memory arrays (address/bool/uint184 cleanup, uint256 copy) stay whiles (P7): maxDeposit, maxMint, reallocate x3, updateWithdrawQueue's event, getWhiteList, getRoleMembers, deposit x2, mint x2. P2 here = 34 'args mem[' lines + 104 selectors shown as mem[_N len 4] + 38 raw Error(string) reverts (first finding). P9: the Taylor expansion of wTaylorCompounded is distributed into polynomials of block.timestamp and lastUpdate (220 lines with 'block.timestamp * block.timestamp'), plus 512-bit mulDiv. P13/def storage: role membership for constant roles becomes separate variables stor1995/stor200E/stor511D/stor9124/storB7DB, hasRole/grantRole with a variable role stay stor[sha3(account, sha3(role, 0x2dd7..))]; whiteList's _values array is 'stor7 is uint256' with data at stor[0xa66c..]; the Initializable slot is split as uint72/uint184 and written as 18446744073709551617 (P15). P11: Panic(50) after length++ (5), 's >= withdrawQueue.length' inside a loop bounded by it, ECDSA error code 2 that tryRecover(v,r,s) never returns. P8: the via-IR keccak scratch (mem[0] = x; mem[0] = base; mem[0] = x) is printed everywhere. Parameter names from the signature database mislead in places (withdraw(uint256 shares, address to, address from) takes assets; withdrawFor's third parameter is the sender, not a receiver; initialize's 'rewards' is the asset).
summary: Faithful, every in-contract loop shown as a while, but long and opaque: inside the inlined totalAssets loop the free-memory pointer is not followed, so Moolah calls, library calls and 'max uint128 exceeded' reverts lose names and arguments; the interest arithmetic is distributed into polynomials, storage strings are open-coded, and role errors and the allocator-or-bot test are printed in confusing forms.
